neighbours.label: 'so' as a degree intensifier before an adjective (so X that ...)
fire: The soup was so salty that nobody finished it.
Her voice sounded so tired that we let her rest.
The exam questions were so confusing that half the class failed.
He spoke in a tone so cold that the room went quiet.
The insult was so crude that the host cut the microphone.
Their apology seemed so sincere that we forgave them.
By dawn the fog had grown so thick that the ferry stopped running.
His remarks were so rude that the meeting ended early.
quiet: The soup was very salty, and nobody finished it.
Her voice sounded tired, so we let her rest.
The exam questions were confusing, and half the class failed.
He spoke in a cold tone and the room went quiet.
The insult was crude, so the host cut the microphone.
Their apology seemed sincere, and we forgave them.
By dawn the fog had thickened and the ferry stopped running.
His remarks were extremely rude and the meeting ended early.
